lines.text: A mechanism is one part of the robot, written as one class. This one's the arm.
In Tuner X, you set this motor up by hand. Generate Code copies those settings out. That copy goes right here, in the constructor.
First, the hardware: the CAN bus, the motor on thirty one, and the CANcoder on thirty two.
When the arm gets built, the constructor sends that config to the motor once. The motor saves it and keeps it.
A request is different. It says what to do right now, and the code sends a new one every loop.
Whichever request arrives last is the one the motor keeps doing. Hold on to that. It comes back in a few lessons.
One setting matters more than it looks. The motor counts its own turns, but that count starts over at zero every time the robot powers on.
Try it. Move the arm, power cycle the robot, and compare the two readings.
The CANcoder remembers the real angle. These lines make it the motor's source, so every angle you ask for later is a real one.
Last, the robot builds the arm once, as a field, and every mode you write uses that same arm.
Settings go in once. Requests go every loop, and the last one sticks.
